subject: EOQ: priority & timeline check StellarApps evaluation
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stellarapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: StellarApps — follow-up & next steps (mutual action plan)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the deep dive on your reporting workloads and the latency goals for the inference-backed features. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Recap: Your main goals are (1) < 150ms tail latency for 95p on short text transforms, (2) predictable monthly spend at scale, and (3) SOC2 evidence for vendor onboarding.
- Proposed initial scope: 3 production routes (web API + batch embedding pipeline + low-priority async job), estimate 2–4 reserved GPUs for peak throughput.
- Action items I’ll take: share mutual action plan & pricing deck (attached), and a short procurement checklist for your security/infra teams.
- Action items for StellarApps: confirm priority (high/medium/low) and whether procurement needs an NDA/PO and who the approvers are. Also, any SSO/KMS constraints?

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, redwood-pricing-deck.pdf

We’re approaching the end of quarter this week — are you still targeting an EOQ decision, or has timing shifted to early July? If EOQ is critical, we can prioritize a short security pack and a legal redline review to speed procurement.

Would you be open to a quick 20-min sync early next week to lock the timeline?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0162

---

(attachment stubs: mutual_action_plan.xlsx [spreadsheet], redwood-pricing-deck.pdf [pdf])

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@stellarapps.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@stellarapps.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StellarApps — follow-up & next steps (mutual action plan)

Thanks Aditya — good recap. A couple quick questions: 

1) Can you confirm the expected monthly spend range (ballpark) for the 2–4 reserved GPU configuration you outlined? We need that for our budget approval form.
2) On the procurement/security front: we typically run a short security questionnaire and a legal PO/term review. I’ll loop Procurement but from a priority standpoint this is currently medium — we have a couple of initiatives ahead of this one for EOQ.

I’ll discuss with Priya and get back to you, but any detail you can share on cost and a suggested procurement checklist would help.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product Ops | StellarApps
alex.turner@stellarapps.com

Hi Alex —

Just bumping this in case it slipped through — wanted to answer your cost question quickly: for the 2–4 reserved GPU profile we discussed, most customers land in the $12k–$28k/month range depending on batching and caching. If you expect heavy synchronous traffic the higher end is more likely; we can model a precise estimate once you share RPS/avg tokens.

If procurement/security needs a concise checklist, Marissa can put together a 1-page pack (SOC2 artifacts, data retention, network/isolation options) and Sean can help map the integration checklist for SSO/KMS. Happy to loop them into a quick call if helpful.

Would you prefer that we set up a procurement intro this week, or should we check back next week? Also: are you still targeting a decision by EoQ or has that priority shifted?

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Priya —

Quick EOQ check-in — hope you’re well. We’re doing a short sweep with a handful of prospects to understand whether timing/budget for ongoing POCs is still on track for EoQ, or if teams are deprioritizing until next quarter. Two quick asks: 

1) Has priority changed since our last note (high / medium / low)?
2) Do you still expect procurement/approval to land before EoQ, or should we plan for an early-July decision window?

If EOQ is important, we can accelerate onboarding materials and offer a legal/PO kickoff to remove blockers this week. If not, no problem — we’ll align on a revised timeline.

Appreciate a quick reply — even a one-line update helps us prioritize resources on our end.

Best,
